title: The saturated spectral radius for complete graphs
summary: A graph is $K_{r+1}$-saturated if it is $K_{r+1}$-free and adding any missing edge creates a copy of $K_{r+1}$. Kim, Kim, Kostochka, and O conjectured that $K_{r-1}\vee(n-r+1)K_1$ minimizes the spectral radius among all $n$-vertex $K_{r+1}$-saturated graphs. They proved the case $r=2$, and the cases $r=3$ and $r\in\{4,5\}$ were subsequently established by Kim, Kostochka, O, Shi, and Wang, and by Wang and Hou, respectively. We settle the conjecture for all $r\ge3$: if $n\ge r+1$ and $G$ is an $n$-vertex $K_{r+1}$-saturated graph, then \[ ρ(G)\ge \frac{r-2+\sqrt{(r-2)^2+4(r-1)(n-r+1)}}{2}, \]…
